subject: Industrial heritage

subject: Former uses of buildings

subject: Former uses of buildings

Their chief was the Grand Bali of the Order and Commander of the Gozo Forts.

subject: Former uses of buildings

name: My Beautiful Laundrette
subject: Filming locations

name: North-East gate of Roman Corinium
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the North-East gate of Roman Corinium where the Fosseway from Lincoln and Akeman Street from Verulamium (St. Albans) entered the town. Excavations in 1960 revealed a gate 30m wide, with flanking towers and a dual-carriage-way of cobbled streets. The River Churn was diverted to flow just outside the town wall.

Elizabeth Sturge, Vice-President and Council member of Redland High School for Girls, helped to create better housing for working people. Founded in 1882, the school stood on this site until 2016 when it merged with The Red Maids’ School to form Redmaids’ High School.

The Black Swan Hotel was "visited" by Sherlock Holmes and Dr Watson in Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's "The Adventure of the Copper Beeches".

This building (formerly the Old Library built 1913) followed in a similar tradition.

name: John Flavel

name: Wellington Court
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Wellington Court Formerly the 'Red Barracks'. Built 1794-1803 at a time of threatened French invasion. Remained in military use over 150 years.

name: Great North of Scotland Railway Company
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: These premises, completed in 1894, were formerly the headquarters of the Great North of Scotland Railway Company. They include the Company's magnificent boardroom. The adjoining Station Hotel was opened in 1900 and acquired by the Company in 1910. Both premises passed to the LNER in 1923, and to British Railways in 1948. They were sold into private ownership in 1983. Presented by the Great North of Scotland Railway Association - November 1994.

name: James Legge

subject: Industrial heritage

text: The Jolly Sailor The name of this public house is a reminder of the nearby River Avon and it situated on High Street, which follows the line of a Roman Road. The earliest recorded landlord was Charles Coole, who was in charge 1853-1874. The Jolly Sailor is a former George's Brewery pub, originally the Old Porter Brewery, established in 1788. George's Brewery closed in 1995.

name: Berwick-upon-Tweed railway station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: The North British Railway built Berwick on Tweed station in 1843, on the site of a 12th century castle. In 1913 it designed a new station, with many Scottish overtones in its design, but the Great War prevented construction until 1924. Thus the London & North Eastern Railway built the present station, with its island platform and footbridge. The station is Listed Grade II.

name: The Star
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Star A tavern has stood on this site since 1832. The present building dates from the 1700’s and remains largely unaltered with all it’s ‘Olde Worlde’ character and charme. In the days when Godalming has over 50 inns and ale houses, six we’re here in Church Street. Now only The Star survives, offering a warm welcome to all who pass this way.

name: The Shambles, Wetherby
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: THE SHAMBLES Built in 1811 by the Duke of Devonshire for butchers shops, each was let for three guineas a year. In 1888 it was converted into an open market which sold poultry and dairy produce. At the beginning of the Great War these shambles were used for miniature rifle practice.

name: St. James Church
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: St. James Church - 1763 Founded in 1546, was originally a chapel of ease for Altham Parish Church. Rebuilt in 1763 and further extended in 1828, became a parish church in 1870 and was completely reroofed in 1993.

name: Mary Erskine School
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: To commemorate the Mary Erskine School which stood on this site from 1871-1966 presented by the former pupils' guild to celebrate their 125th anniversary - June 2009.

name: Llandudno railway station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Opened originlly in 1858 by the Chester & Holyhead railway, the station was rebuilt by the London and North Western Railway in 1892 to serve increasing levels of holiday traffic. In the 1970s the station was radically reduced in size as a result of changing travel trends. Restored in 2014, the station sits in the Llandudno Town Centre & Seafront Conservation Area.

name: Sun Inn, Hemel Hempstead
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: 81 High Street Formerly the Sun Inn, it was the meeting place for the Artisans' Benefit Society from 1775. The Sun finally closed in 1960.

name: Henry Cubbon
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Master Mariner These licensed premises form part of Union Terrace, originally a short row of lodging houses built for the seaside resort of New Brighton, created in the 1830's. Henry Cubbon, 'Master Mariner', was one of the Terrace's early residents. Captain Cubbon died in 1855, aged 40. His death was announced in the Liverpool Mercury. By the 20th century the lodging houses had been converted into cafes and public houses.

name: John Lennon
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: 'The Beatles' played here, their first performance in Wales, formerly the Regent Dansette Ballroom, Rhyl on Saturday 14th July 1962.

name: Sybil Thorndike
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Thorndike Theatre was designed by Roderick Ham and named after the actress Dame Sybil Thorndike. It was opened in 1969 by Princess Margaret. Formerly the site of the Crescent Cinema, the Thorndike replaced the old repertory theatre at No. 27 High Street, whcih itself had also previously been a cinema. The theatre was reopened as The Leatherhead Theatre in April 2001 and had been staging productions ever since.

name: Saint Mary Magdalen Church
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Four churches dedicated to Saint Mary Magdalen have stood on this site purchased from Joseph LeBlanc by Père Mégret in 1843. The present church was built in 1911 under the pastorate of Père Laforest.

subject: Industrial heritage
text: Constructed by the Midland Railway to designs in the Neo-Baroque style by company architect Charles Trubshaw, with external detail by local architect Albert Edward Lambert, and opened in January 1904. The station is Grade II* listed. Major refurbishment of the station took place in 2014 in conjunction with the extension of the Nottingham tram system.

name: Swan Inn, Burnley
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Swan Inn Originally a farmhouse, this building was converted into an inn towards the end of the 18th Century. Here a Town Committee, a forerunner of the Council, met during the years 1816 - c.1844. Behind the inn can be seen part of the liock-up, or jail, opened by the Town Committee in 1819.

name: Middlesbrough Railway Station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Designed in 1877 by W. Peachey, Architect and W.J. Cudworth, Engineer, for the North-Eastern Railway; originall included a two-bay trainshed over inner concourse and platforms, demolished following enemy action in 1942. Listed Grade II.

subject: Industrial heritage

name: Hebden Old Bridge
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Hebden Old Bridge erected circa AD 1510 replacing a medieval bridge built of timber. Many repairs were necessary in AD 1602 and again in AD 1657. The parapet being repared in AD 1845 and raised in AD 1890. The eastern arch of the bridge spans the tail-goit of Bridge Mill, originally the manorial corn-mill of Wadsworth.

name: George Whitefield
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: George Whitefield 1714-1770 preached publicly at this site (formerly the King's Head) 8th February 1739. This was the first time on non-church premises at the start of the "Great Awakening".

name: Copps' Royal Hotel
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Site of Copps' Royal Hotel (1827) Originally the Balcony Boarding House (1810) renamed Copps' Royal Hotel (1819). Demand was such that the hotel was rebuilt in 1827. Reputedly one of the largest in Europe at the time it had 100 beds and stabling for 50 horses and 40 carriages. However, it went bankrupt in 1841 and was empty until it was demolished to make way for the railway in 1847.

It has traded under several other names including the Board, the Hare and Hounds, the Croft Fox, and the Crown Inn. The cellar of the Pub has a capped smugglers tunnel and is next to Bull Lane, one of the oldest surviving alleys that runs to the River Bank. Nowadays, it is famous for its Real Ale and a vibrant local music scene.

subject: Industrial heritage

name: John Bunyan

name: Swanswell Gate

Originally named Priory Gate it gave access to the Prior's lands outside the wall. Including Swanswell Fishpool. The archways were blocked, windows inserted and the roof raised when it was converted into a house and gardens were presented to the city and wall remains are now Scheduled Ancient Monuments.

name: Duke of Wellington Hotel, Rochdale
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Duke of Wellington Hotel (former) Grade II Listed c.1750 Originally a wealthy wool merchant's residence, this building became the Duke of Wellington Hotel in 1810, and was the leading coach house in Rochdale for many years. In front of this hotel, the "Speaker's Corner" hosted a crowd of 8,000 following the Reform Act of 1832.

name: Rougemont

Vlieland. Esq.MD) on the 2nd April in that year. Originally the ditch of Rougemont Castle the grounds formed part of the estate of the Duchy of Cornwall from A.D. 1337 to A.D. 1798.

name: Samuel Taylor Coleridge

name: Golden Ball

name: Wye Bridge
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The bridge was built in 1490 damaged in the Civil War and widened in 1826. There was originally a gatehouse on the southern end which was demolished in 1782.

name: Samuel Pepys
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Formerly the Swann Inn, this building held pride of place among Stevenage inns. Samuel Pepys stayed here in 1667 and it was reputed to be the first stop for couples from London, on their way north to Gretna Green.

name: Globe Inn
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Stood on this site. It was opened in 1798 by David Morris. Among the noted guests during the National Road era were five presidents of the U.S. Lafayette was entertained here on May 25, 1825.

name: George Washington
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: A two-story stone house occupied as a tavern by William Morrow stood on this site. George Washington, with staff, lodged here, Oct. 12, 1794, when traveling west to review troops assembled at Bedford to suppress the Whiskey Rebellion.

name: George Washington
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Home of Gen. Ephraim Blaine, Commissary General of Revolutionary Army, stood on this site. George Washington was a guest here, Oct. 4-11, 1794, while mustering an armed force to quell Whiskey Rebellion in Western Pennsylvania.

name: Fort Lafayette
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Stood on this site. It was completed in 1792. Built to protect Pittsburgh against Indian attacks and to serve as a chief supply base for Gen. Wayne's army, 1792-94. Reactivated during the War of 1812. Site sold in 1813.

name: Thaddeus Stevens
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Lawyer, congressman, abolitionist, ironmaster, and defender of free public schools in Pennsylvania, lived in a house that stood on this site. He moved from here in 1842.

name: workhouse, Haverfordwest
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: A Workhouse called Priory Mount was built on this site during 1837-1839. It continued in use until the Second World War when it became a hospital, subsequently serving as a unit of The County Hospital and Withybush General Hospital. It was converted into flats in 1982.

name: Whitmore Railway Station Booking Office
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Once the main station for North Staffordshire on the Grand Junction Railway opened in 1837. On 29th June 1937 The Coronation engine, no.6220, recorded 114 mph north of Whitmore.

name: Albion Hotel, Arnside
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Built about 1810 originally as a house for a Captain Greenwood, mariner and ship owner. On his death in 1854 control passed to his son-in-law Richard Bush, who turned the house into Bush's Albion Hotel as shipping declined. Under various owners it has remained a hotel ever since.

name: Frank Matcham
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: A Theatre has stood on this site since 1776. The current building was designed by the famous theatre architect Frank Matcham (1854-1920) and opened on 15th October 1894. This Grade II* Listed Building is Matcham's smallest surviving theatre in the British Isles.

name: City Court Designed by G.B.H
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: City Court Designed by G.B.H. Austin of the Public Works Department and built by Swanston Bros in 1911, the building originally accommodated three large courtrooms and offices with a two storey octagonal main vestibule. The facades, faced in Moorabool sandstone, focus on the entrance where gables, turrets, and arches produce an exceptional Romanesque composition.

name: 20 Park Parade
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: In 1796, this building was converted into a Methodist Chapel, later becoming a club house. From 1890-1912 it was the home and studio of Bernard Evans RA, the celebrated water colourist.

name: James W
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: James W. Latimer (Weck). (1783 - 1860) Latimer was born in New London, Conn. Moved to Texas, with family, in 1833. Founder and editor first newspaper in Dallas, 1849. Known originally as "The Cedar Snag" then as "Dallas Herald." Incorporated into "Dallas Morning News" in 1885. Recorded, 1968 #6757.

name: Tate-Senftenberg-Brandon Home
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Originally a modest one-story cottage built about 1867 by Phocian Tate. Sold in 1887 to A. Senftenberg, merchant, who added second story and porches with Victorian ornamentation. In 1900 Kenneth Brandon bought home and extended northeast section. Most of early features still remain. Of interest is basement built of Columbus-made brick. In 1968 Magnolia Homes Tour bought house to restore it as a museum, with period furnishings. #5205.

name: Replica of XIT's Giant Windmill
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Yellowhouse division of 3,050,000-acre XIT Ranch built (1887) a 132-foot windmill southwest of here. Set in a canyon, it had to be tall to catch breezes and pump water. It was known as the world's tallest windmill until it was toppled by winds in 1926. This replica was erected May 27, 1969. (1970) #4248.

name: First United Methodist Church of Morgan
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: First United Methodist Church of Morgan. Organized in 1889, the Morgan Methodist Church first held worship services in the Baptist church building. At an 1891 revival, the fellowship initiated plans to construct this sanctuary. Originally a one-room structure, the building was enlarged in later years as additional rooms were needed. The Carpenter Gothic building exhibits some Greek Revival detailing and features lancet windows and a 1901-02 belfry. Recorded Texas Historic Landmark - 1983 #1892.

name: Thomas Telford
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Corbet Arms This hotel, originally a 17th Century coaching inn was known as "The Talbot" until 1825. Thomas Telford stayed here in 1832 during the building of teh nearby canal. An important town meeting place, in 1862 it was the scene of the inauguration of the Nantwich and Market Drayton Railway.

name: Robert Harvey Cox
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the house, and at the rear, the fusee watch chain workshop, of Robert Harvey Cox 1754-1815 who introduced the industry to the town in the 1790s. The manufacture which used factory, cottage and workhouse labour, continued in the town until 1914.
area: Christchurch, Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole, England

name: Whitby Railway Station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Whitby Railway Station opened 1847 and built to the design of George T. Andrews architect to the York & North Midland Railway Company.

name: Low Mill Foundry
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Low Mill Foundry, owned by WM.Smith & Co., stood on this site from 1869 - 1991. The company, which began in 1867, took the name of "Low" Mill from its original premises which had been a riverside watermill, situated lower downstream than Barnard Castle's other industrial sites.

name: Old Blue Bell Inn, Gosport
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: "The Old Blue Bell Inn" stood on this site for almost 300 years. Close by was the workshop of James Philpot who, in 1589, produced the earliest recorded book to be printed in Hampshire.

name: Banbury Blue Coat School
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: St. Mary's C of E Primary School Formerly the Blue Coat School Situated in the Market Place Founded 1705.

name: Kilmore Mechanics' Institute and Free Library
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: This plaque was installed on 15 October 2005 to mark the 150th anniversary of the Kilmore Mechanics Institute and Free Library whose Hall stood on this site 1863-1978.

name: Halifax Town Association Football Club
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the Saddle Hotel where the Association Football Club Halifax Town was established on 23rd May 1911.

name: Chesterfield Railway Station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: North Midland House designed by Francis Thompson Built 1840 Sole surviving building of Chesterfield's first railway station.

name: The Palace, Rushden
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood The Palace September 1910 - November 1956 Rushden's first cinema.

name: Arthur Melbourne-Cooper
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the Alpha Cinematograph Works studio of film pioneer Arthur Melbourne-Cooper (1874-1961).

name: Preston Railway Station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Designed by the architects Cooper and Tullis of Preston for the London and North Western and the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railways, the joint station was completed in 1880, replacing Preston's first station on the same site dating from 1838 with later additions. Listed Grade II.

name: Vintage House, Seaton
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Built by John Head, Seaton's first major property developer - originally as 2 gentleman's houses for his sons.

name: The Railway Children
subject: Filming locations
text: The classic film The Railway Children was filmed at Oakworth Station 1970.

name: Mary Wollstonecraft
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the cottage (mentioned in Frankenstein) visited by Mary Wollstonecraft Godwin 1812 - 1814.

name: Joseph Lister
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the surgical wards in which from 1861 to 1869 Joseph Lister surgeon to the Royal Infirmary and Regius Professor of Surgery in the University of Glasgow initiated the method of antiseptic treatment.

name: Thirsk Infant School
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: This building was formerly the Thirsk Infant School founded by public subscription and erected in 1833 on a site donated by John Bell Lord of the Manor. It was opened as a Public Library by N.Y.C.C. in 1981.

name: Ilkley Railway Station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Opened in 1865, the Otley & Ilkley Joint Railway helped Ilkley's growth as a tourist and dormitory town. The line extended to Skipton from 1888 until 1965. A public campaign saved the railway to Leeds and Bradford.

name: Eastbrook Chapel
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the Eastbrook Chapel a christian meeting place opened in 1825 with seating for 1500.

name: John Wesley
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: From May 1747 onwards John Wesley on several occasions visited this locality staying at the old Booth Bank Farm, Agden and preaching under the oak tree still in front of the house The above plaque was affixed to the Booth Bank Methodist Chapel which stood on this site from 1834 The building was demolished in 1972.

name: Smethwick Public Building
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Originally the Smethwick Public Building Built in 1867 by the Local Board of Health and used as the main library since 1928.

name: Parrett Works 19th C
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Parrett Works 19th C. Built in 1854 on the site of old Cary's Mill, mentioned in the Doomsday Book, this was originally a flour mill, then a flax mill and canvas and rope makers, later manufacturing engineering products. More than 300 persons were employed here at its prime.

name: Adam Smith
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Adam Smith 1723-1790 born in Kirkcaldy. On this site stood the home of his mother in which he lived from 1767 - 1776 and completed 'The Wealth Of Nations'. House removed 1834. His grave is in the Canongate Churchyard, Edinburgh. Erected 1953.

name: George Inn, Bridport
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: No 9 East Street This building originally The George Inn was rebuilt by renowned local Apothecary Dr Giles Roberts in 1804. It was a Pharmacy until 1974.

name: Town Hall, Bournemouth
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Town Hall Buildings 1875 Sir George Tapps built the thatched "Ashley Cottages" here in 1812. In 1875 Bournemouth's first Town Hall was built on this site. The civic offices, which later became the Criterion Hotel, survive at the front, but with an 1898 facade. The hall was converted into an arcade in 1886 and refurbished in 1962 and 1991.
area: Bournemouth, Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole, England

name: Coloured Cloth Hall, Leeds
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Coloured Cloth Hall Leeds' most splendid Georgian cloth hall, built in 1758, stood on this site. Projecting to the centre of City Square, its massive quandrangular structure housed 1770 stalls for clothiers selling dyed woollen cloth at the Tuesday and Saturday markets.

name: 48 Middlebridge Street Built circa 1700
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: 48 Middlebridge Street Built circa 1700. Formerly a wool warehouse. Converted to the Elite Cinema early 20th century.

name: Liverpool Road railway station, Manchester
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Liverpool Road Station Opened 15 September 1830. Treminus of the Liverpool & Manchester Railway and the world's oldest surviving railway station.

name: Clement Clarke Moore
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: In the Moore Mansion, which stood on this site, in 1822, Clement Clarke Moore, (1779-1863), penned the immortal poem, "A Visit From Saint Nicholas", (T'was The Night Before Christmas), as a gift for his children. Scholar and developer of modern Chelsea, he gave the land for St. Peter's Church and the General Theological Seminary, where he was Professor of Greek and Hebrew.

name: Gillygate, Pontefract
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The street leading to St. Giles Church and formerly the main approach to the town from the south.

name: David Lean
subject: Filming locations
text: Sir David Lean (1908-1991) director of many famous British films including Brief Encounter filmed here in 1945.

name: James Joyce
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood Ireland's very first dedicated picture house, the Volta Cinema. It was opened on 20th December 1909 and managed by James Joyce. The converted 420-seat venue was renamed the Lyceum in 1921. It closed in 1948 and was demolished in the 1960s. Only the upper floor facades survives.

name: Middlesbrough Winter Garden
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Winter Garden founded by Sir Hugh and Lady Bell for the benefit of the people of Middlesbrough stood on this site 1907-1963.

name: Charles Dickens
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Charles Dickens 1812-1870 was a frequent visitor to the Bedford Hotel which stood on this site until 1964.

name: Chariots of Fire
subject: Filming locations
text: The memorable beach scene from Chariots of Fire was filmed here 1981.

name: Crown Inn, Cobham
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Here stood the Crown Inn, demolished c.1913. The adjoining footpath, which is called Crown Alley, was originally a track leading into Church Field, one of Cobham's open fields in medieval times.

name: William Bailey
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: This house, formerly the 'Champneys Arms' inn and London coach office, was built in 1739 by William Bailey, joiner, under lease from Richard Champneys, of Orchardleigh 1739-1989.

name: Samuel Johnson
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood Dame Oliver's Infant School where Dr. Samuel Johnson was taught English 1714. Born 1709. Died 1784.

name: Glencairn Greit House
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Glencairn Greit House 1623 Formerly the town residence of the Earl of Glencairn and of the Duke of Argyll. Acquited by the Town Council of Dumbarton in 1924.

name: Moor Street railway station, Birmingham
subject: Industrial heritage
text: To Commemorate the Centenary of Moor Street station opened on the 1st July 1909 1909-2009.

name: Leamington Spa railway station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: This Art Deco station was opened in 1939 by the Great Western Railway to replace the original building of 1852. Restoration of the booking hall carried out by Chiltern Railways with the support of the Friends of Leamington Station, Royal Leamington Spa Town Council and the Railway Heritage Trust, was completed in 2008. This station is listed Grade II.

name: Ladysmith Barracks
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Ladysmith Barracks An army barracks has stood on this site since 1845. It was the home of the Manchester Regiment from 1881-1958.

name: Arthur Thompson
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: A. Thompson & Co: From 1922 to 1983 Mr. Arthur Thompson and his son Mr. Kenneth Thompson rendered service to the people of Rowlands Gill from the garage which formerly stood on this site.

name: William Clarke
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: William Clarke (1831-1890) Industrialist and Co-Founder of Clarke Chapman lived in the Hermitage, which stood on this site.

name: Paragon railway station, Hull
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Opened in 1848 and substantially enlarged to a design by William Bell in 1904, Paragon Station was the principal Hull passenger station of the North Eastern Railway which, with its dock, cartage, hotel and shipping interests, was a major local employer.
area: Hull, Kingston upon Hull, City of, England

name: William Wordsworth
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the grammar school which William Wordsworth Poet Laureate attended as a boy. To this school also came Fletcher Christian leader of the Mutiny On The Bounty April 28th 1788.

name: Philip Crewe
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: This building incorporates the Shoemakers guildhall. Left to the Guild in 1683 by Philip Crewe in memory of his father.

name: John Wallis
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Bedford Hotel Formerly the Royal Marine Library of John Wallis, Bookseller by Appointment to the Duke and Duchess of Kent. Established here c. 1813. Publisher, bookseller and business associate of R Ackerman of Strand, London. Much knowledge of early 19th C. Sidmouth comes from Wallis's publications and topographical prints. The Library was badly damaged in the great storm of 22nd Nov 1824, the Wallis family only just escaping.

name: Maritime Hotel, Belfast
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Maritime Hotel birthplace of Rhythm 'n' Blues in Belfast April 1964 stood on this site.

name: Turgesius Tower
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Turgesius Tower c 1000 AD built by the Vikings stood on this site.

name: Billy Liar
subject: Filming locations
text: Billy Liar the classic comedy of the Swinging Sixties was filmed here 1962.

name: Otley Mechanics' Institute
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Formerly the Mechanics Institute opened 31st Oct. 1871 and extended in 1895.

name: Drill Hall, Perth
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The Drill Hall - 1915 The Army Drill Hall that stood on this site was used by the 11/44 Battalion, Red Cross Voluntary Aid Detachment and Cadet Corps as a training and social centre. The property extended to Keightley Road and included a parade ground. The Drill Hall was sold in 1989.

name: H. F. Hodges
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: The site was originally the ground of Oxford City Football Club, and H.F. Hodges was the scorer of the first goal when Oxford City won the Amateur Cup in 1906.

name: James Tissot
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the Royal Albion Hotel, James J. J. Tissot, 1836-1902 artist stayed and painted here in 1876.

name: Charles I
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Star and Garter stood here rebuilt 1836 coaching inn formerly an Elizabethan house where King Charles I stayed 17 October 1642.

name: Worthing railway station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: This building was opened by The London & South Coast Railway as the first Worthing station on November 25th 1845 Threatened with demolition in 1971 Later restored by Frank Sandell & Sons (Worthing) Limited in 1988.

name: Thomas Tucker
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Built in the 1790's and known originally as West End House. It was built as the dower house for the mother of Gustaves Ducarel, the squire of the now demolished Manor House in Manor Gardens. In 1801 Richard Webber astonished the town by buying the house and converting it into a shop. The original shop front is incorporated in the present frontage.

name: Town Hall, Beccles
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Town Hall (Grade II) Built in 1765, in Gothic Revival style on the site of the old Market Cross, originally with an octagonal turret over the doorway Formerly the Shire Hall and Courthouse, it is now the Town Hall.

name: Market Cross, Wymondham
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Market Cross Built 1618 to replace a former cross destroyed in the Great Fire of 1615. Formerly the Market Clerk's office, this later became the Council chamber and reading room.

name: Wymondham railway station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Railway station built 1845 on the Norwich to Brandon Railway, later the G.E.R. and L.N.E.R. line to London. Restored 1989 by David Turner.

name: Pitmuxton House
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood Pitmuxton House. In 1309 Pitmuxton was granted by Robert The Bruce to Hugo of Aberdeen carrying with it the royal office of Mayor of Fee collector of the King's revenues.

name: John Phillip
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: On this site stood the house where on 19th April 1817 John Phillip RA was born.

name: Black Boy Inn, Chelmsford
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Upon this site stood the Black Boy Inn which played a central role in Chelmsford life for three centuries to 1857.

name: Romsey railway station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: ROMSEY STATION Built by the London & South Western Railway. First passenger train and steam locomotive 'Eclipse' arrived March 1st 1847. Platforms extended and subway added 1886. Troops left from here for France in the wars of 1914-1918 and 1939-1945.

name: The Manor House, Ilkley
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Originating in the 14th century and formerly known as The Castle, this mainly 17th century house was built on the remains of the Roman Fort. By 1804 it was divided into cottages. In 1955 it was saved from demolition when Percy Dalton donated it to the community. It was converted into the Art Gallery and Museum in 1961.

name: Curzon Street railway station, Birmingham
subject: Industrial heritage
text: This plaque commemorates the 150th anniversary of the arrival of the first London to Birmingham train at this station on Monday 17th September 1838.

name: William Gibbs School for Girls
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Formerly the William Gibbs School for Girls founded in 1883 by Richard Gibbs in memory of his father William Gibbs. Merged with the Boys' Grammar School in 1967 and converted into flats in 1994.

name: Lytham St Annes railway station
subject: Industrial heritage
text: Built in 1874 when the Blackpool-Lytham line was joined to the Lytham-Kirkham branch of the Preston and Wyre Railway. It fell out of use after downgrading by British Rail. The Italianate stone facade was preserved during conversion to a pub in 1986.

name: Clement Cramp
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Old Coffee Tavern Formerly a temperance coffee house with reading room Built c1890 by Clement Cramp (1816 - 1894) for working men.

name: Greyfriars
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: A Franciscan friary, know as the Greyfriars, stood on this site from 1224 until 1538. A substantial mansion called "The Friars" followed. In 1846 the London, Brighton and South Coast Railway built a station here. Passenger traffic ceased in 1857 and it was demolished in 1967.

name: William Harrison Ainsworth
subject: Former uses of buildings
text: Harrison Ainsworth 1805-1883 novelist was born in a house which stood on this site.

name: Clock Tower
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The Clock Tower Built in 1873 This building housed the local fire station until 1915.

name: John Noel Nichols
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: A Monument to Vimto by Kerry Moisen 1992 Stamed Oak taken from a managed forest John Noel Nichols mixed his first batch of Vimto at 19 Granby Row in 1908 This sculpture on the site ofl the building was commissioned at J N Nichols (Vimto) plc.

name: Alexander Keiller
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The Alexander Keiller Museum This museum was founded by the late Alexander Keiller of Morven and opened in 1938 as the Morven Institute of Archaeological Research. It houses the material from his excavations at Windmill Hill and Avebury between the years 1925 and 1939, material which his widow, Mrs Gabrielle Keiller, gave to the nation in 1966.

name: Joseph Priestley
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: International Historic Chemical Landmark Bowood House Joseph Priestley (1733-1804) - Unitarian minister, teacher, author and natural philosophe - was the Earl of Sherburne's librarian and tutor to his sons. In this room, then a working laboratory, Priestley pursued his investigations of gases. On 1 August 1774 he discovered oxygen. Twenty years later he emigrated to America where he continued his research at his home and laboratory in Northumberland. Pennsylvania.

name: K Shop
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: From the 1870's this building contained K Shop (coppersmiths); the white metal shop, and the brass shop and store - through it incorporates two earlier buildings of the 1846 Wagon Works (These earlier buildings were built of pier-and-panel construction as can be seen).

name: Abraham Compton
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Abraham Compton 1649-1724 donor of the land for this the first Non-conformist Chapel in Chorley 1725.

name: Wren House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: An early Georgian clothier's house built c.1720-30, featuring a Venetian window and six-panel door with a Gibbs surround.

name: William Jackson Hooker
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Sir William Jackson Hooker 1785-1865 Botanist & first director of the Royal Botanic Gardens (Kew) was born here.

name: David Milne (artist)
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The painter and printmaker David Milne (1882-1953) lived here from 1939 to 1940.

name: Raymond Moriyama
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: 71 Front Street East 1982 Designed by the renowned Canadian firm Moriyama & Teshima Architects, this mixed-use building opened when the St. Lawrence area was undergoing urban renewal. It features a large sunlit atrium with a landscaped watercourse.

name: Glasgow Subway
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Former Ticket Office of the Glasgow Subway opened 1896 and the 3rd-oldest underground metro in the world. A 6½ mile circuit; cable-hauled until electrified in 1935.

name: Decimus Burton
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Lower Lighthouse Completed 1840 Designed by Decimus Burton and Capt. H.M. Denham. This land-based lighthouse, the Pharos and Wyre Light, brought vessels safely into port.

name: Eastern Region Best Station Competition 1987
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Eastern Region Best Station Competition 1987. This is to certify that Cambridge station was awarded first prize in the 1987 Best Station Competition (large station category).

name: Christopher Layer
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Christopher Layer of Boston lived here. He was a faithful adherent of the House of Stuart and for his loyalty to that cause suffered an ignominious death at Tyburn 17 May 1723. This tablet was placed here to perpetuate his memory Dec 1908. Be thou faithful unto death.

name: Public Hall
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This building was opened in 1901 as the town's main meeting place. It replaced the Corn Exchange which had burned down in 1898. The basement of the Hall contains part of one of many malt barns found in Jedburgh until the 18th century. It also housed the town armoury.

name: Murthly Terrace
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: 1862-65 built in baronial style for Sir William Stewart of Murthly.

name: John Rennie
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Wyre Aqueduct A Single Span Aqueduct, 110 Feet Long, Carrying The Canal 34 Feet Above The River Wyre. Engineer: John Rennie First Used 1797.

name: Masonic Hall, Cheltenham
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Cheltenham Masonic Hall 1823 designed and built by George Allen Underwood architect and freemason (1793-1829).

name: Thomas Chalmers
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Theologian, philanthropist, academic. Instrumental in forming the Free Church of Scotland. Lived here 1834 - 1847.

name: Andrew "Jock" Wemyss
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Co-founder of Haddington Rugby Football Club (1931) & The Co-Optimist Rugby Club (1924). Scotland Internationalist. Rugby Journalist & Commentator. War veteran. Lived here.

name: Banbury Civic Society/Talyllyn Railway Preservation Society
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Banbury Civic Society/Talyllyn Railway Preservation Society. This building was formerly Bill Trinder's radio shop. Founder member and first chairman of the Talyllyn Railway Preservation Society (Est. 11th October 1950) In this shop W.G. (Bill) Trinder and L.T.C. (Tom) Rolt resolved to preserve and run the Talyllyn Railway, which became the first railway in the world to be owned and operated by volunteers, whose first train ran on 14th May 1951.

name: The Silver Swallow bridge built 2018
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The Silver Swallow bridge built 2018. Opened September 28 2020 by HRH The Princess Royal. Celebrating 20 years of Telford.

name: Guglielmo Marconi
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Guglielmo Marconi 1874-1937 Founded the Marconi Wireless Telegraph Company Ltd in 1900 Stayed here at the Saracen's Head Hotel whilst visiting his New Street factory between 1912 and 1928 On 15th June 1920 Dame Nellie Melba made the first professional British public wireless broa broadcast from Chelmsford.

name: The Old Station
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The Station, with this elegant porte-cochère, was built in 1847 by Abraham Pattinson who went on to build much of Windermere village. Following engineering and financial difficulties, oppposition from landowners and William Wordsworth, the railway terminated here at Birthwaite instead of at Low Wood nearer to Ambleside. The building was converted to its present use by EH Booth & Co Ltd in 1985.

name: Haverfordwest Station Gateway Improvements 2002
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Undertaken by Pembrokeshire County Council in association with Wales & Borders Trains and Railtrack Plc. Funded by the Welsh Assembly Government, Welsh Development Agency and the Strategic Rail Authority. Opened by Sue Essex AM, Minister for Environment on Wednesday 24th April 2002.

name: Magnus Volk
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Opened in 1883 by Brighton-born inventor and engineer Magnus Volk. The oldest operational electric railway in the world.

name: Th'owd Towser
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Th'owd Towser This building, on the site of the original church lock-up built in or soon after 1597, has been used as a jail, ambulance station, mortuary and fire station.

name: The city and county of Swansea
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The city and county of Swansea. Swansea Transport Package Swansea Railway Station Intermodal Transport Interchange. Opened by the Right Worshipful The Lord Mayor of the City and County of Swansea Councillor Lawrence Bailey on 3rd March 2004.

name: World's First ROYAL ENFIELD Motorcycle
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Designed by Bob Walker Smith, Jules Gobiet. Hunt End Works 1901 WC 0131.

name: Ludlow Travel Centre 2002
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Undertaken by Wales & Borders Trains in association with First Engineering Ltd. Funded by the Strategic Rail Authority and Shropshire County Council. Opened by Richard Bowker, Chairman of the Strategic Rail Authority on Saturday 2 November 2002.

name: Nelly Thornton 1880 - 1915
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Nelly Thornton 1880 - 1915. Model for the Rolls Royce Spirit of Ecstasy Lived here.

name: Institution of Mechanical Engineers
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Bromsgrove Railway Station. Celebrating the 175th Anniversary of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. In 1846 near this spot a group of engineers decided to form an Institution to "give an impulse to inventions likely to be useful to the world." The Institution held its first meeting in Birmingham the following year. 11th May 2022.

name: William Newzam Prior Nicholson
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Sir William 1872‒1949 and Mabel Pryde Nicholson 1871‒1918, artists, lived here 1909‒15.

name: The FA
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: To commemorate the first home game of the England women's senior team. Played at Manor Park Nuneaton Borough FC. England v Scotland Saturday 23 June 1973. Organised by The WFA.

name: Millicent Garrett Fawcett
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Dame Millicent Garrett Fawcett 1847‒1929, suffrage pioneer. Celebrated gaining the first votes for women in this hall on 12th April 1918.

name: Mary of Teck
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The English Bridge was built in 1768 - 1774 on the site of an earlier bridge. In 1925-1927 it was taken down and completely rebuilt. It's steep gradient halved, it's width increased by 126½ feet and every sound stone in the original strucutre reused. The bridge was opened by Her Majesty the Queen on the 13th August 1927.

name: Middlesbrough Football Club
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Middlesbrough Football Club Founded in 1876, Middlesbrough Football Club has played at the Riverside Stadium since 1995. These gates originally formed part of the Boro's former Ayresome Park home (1903 - 1995).

name: William Moon
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: William Moon LLD (1818-1894) lived in this house. Dr. William Moon, himself blind, was the inventor of the special embossed alphabet which bears his name and was designed to enable the blind to read by touch. his pioneer educational and welfare activities are still continued today by the Blatchington Court Trust and the Brighton Society for the Blind.

name: This renovated station was opened b Mrs
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This renovated station was opened b Mrs. Ivy Robbins Saturday 9th. October 1993.

name: Powderhall Stables
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Baronial-style stables built in 1893 for horses hauling Edinburgh's refuse to the adjacent waste incinerator - the Powderhall Destructor.

name: KINGSGATE FOOTBRIDGE
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Mature Concrete Structures Award 1993. Opened November 1963. University of Durham.

name: Thomas Cook
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Travel Pioneer. Cook's very first organised excursion from Leicester to Loughborough arrived here on platform 1 July 1841.

name: Spencer John Bent
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: In memory of Spencer John Bent VC MM 1891-1977 who lived here.

name: John Logie Baird
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Television first demonstrated by John Logie Baird from experiments started here in 1924.

name: Exeter Temporary War Hospital
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: 1915-1919 This building was used as Exeter Temporary War Hospital No 5 for the treatment of sick and injured soldiers in the First World War.

name: Norman Angell
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Sir Norman Angell 1872-1967 Author and Lecturer awarded Nobel Peace Prize 1933 Was born here.

name: Wimborne Workhouse
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Wimborne Workhouse built 1760 on this site For the relief of the poor and infirm. Demolished 1958.

name: Young Men's Evening Institute
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built as a Young Men's Evening Institute 1903. Funded by Charlotte and Ada Phipps. Towcester Studio Band founded here 1910.

name: David Hinde
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Appointed 2012 David Hinde Member of Ancient & Honourable Guild Of Town Criers Bridlington's First Town Crier Since 1901.
area: Bempton, East Riding of Yorkshire, England

name: Hinckley station
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: These refurbished buildings and new offices were opened on 17th May 1990 by His Worship The Mayor, Councillor R.W. Watchorn, Hinckley and Bosworth Council.

name: Zoltan Lewinter-Frankl
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Zoltan and Anny Lewinter-Frankl 1894-1961 and 1908-1999 Patrons of the Arts and Entrepreneurs lived here.

name: John Deyell
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Surveyor and pioneer Born in Drum, he emigrated to Canada and founded the village of Millbrook, Ontario.

name: Tom Hullat
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Tom Hullat, Tibshelf athlete, came third in Roger Bannister's first sub-four-minute mile at Oxford on 6th May 1954.

name: Thomas Bacon
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The school built in 1819 on the site where Thomas Bacon lived. His cottage was destroyed after the revolution.

name: Hermann Ebbinghaus
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: One of the oldest houses in Seaford. Hermann Ebbinghaus 1850-1909 pioneer psychologist lived here.

name: E. M. Forster
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: E.M. Forster. novelist, 1879-1970. Lived here sometimes at the home of his friends Robert and May Buckingham and died here on 7 June 1970. Erected to mark the 100th anniversary of his birth.

name: Harry F. Welsh
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Band of Brothers Richard 'Dick' Winters Harry F Welsh Lived here 1943-1944 Easy Company 506th P.I.R. 101st Airborne Division.

name: Slindon Airfield
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: In memory of Slindon Airfield opened 28.04.1918 closed 30.01.1919. Dedicated to all units and personnel based here.

name: Philip Doddridge
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built 1695. Enlarged 1842. United with Commercial St Church 1959. United Reformed Church 1972. Castle Hill United Reformed Church. Formerly Congregational, Doddridge & Commerical Street U.R.C. Scene of the ministry of Revd. Philip Doddridge AD 1729-51.

name: George Yeomans Pocock
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: George Yeomans Pocock 1891-1976 Master builder of racing boats in Eton and Seattle and champion sculler lived here 1901-1905.

name: Auberge d'Italie
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built in 1574. Enlarged in 1683. This building was occupied by the Italian Knights of St John who were entrusted with the defence of St Peter and Pauls's Bastions. Their chief was the Admiral of the Order.

name: Frederick H. Trimble
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Carey Hand Funeral Home 36 West Pine Street Carey Hand came to Orlando in 1907 and bought his father's embalming business in 1914. He opened this funeral home in 1920, designed by architect F.H. Trimble in the Tuscan style with a chapel, the first of its kind in Florida. The crematorium, built in 1925, was the first in the entire South. The Carey Hand Funeral Home operated here until 1987.

name: Charles McDuffie
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built in 1935 by Charles McDuffie and first occupied by Thomas & Dorothy McElhiney, this California Ranch house contributes to the Monte Vista & College View Historic District.

name: At this spot H.R.H
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: At this spot H.R.H. Prince Alfred tipped the first truck of stone for the breakwater on the 17th of September 1860.

name: “The Birdcages”
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The Legislative Buildings for the Colony of Vancouver Island were built on these grounds in 1859. Nicknamed “The Birdcages” because of their quaint style, they were replaced in 1894-97 by the present buildings. The original Legislative Hall, meeting place of the first House of Assembly west of the Great Lakes, was preserved until 1957 when it was destroyed by fire.

name: Oliver St John Gogarty
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Oliver St John Gogarty. 1878 - 1957. Poet and Surgeon. Lived here.

name: Kentucky An Iroquois word meaning Meadow Land
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Kentucky An Iroquois word meaning Meadow Land. It was visited by Indian tribes from as far west as the Rocky Mountains before 1750. The first white settlement was at Harrodsburg in 1774. Kentucky was the second district west of the Alleghenies to be settled and the first (1792) to become a state.

name: City of Carrollton
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Carrollton incorporated June 14, 1913, with a 52-23 vote. A city council was elected July 19, 1913. With 40 votes, William Forest Vinson was elected as Carrollton's first mayor. Vinson, who also served as the presiding officer of the election, school board trustee, precinct chairman and Dallas County sheriff, declined the office. August 5, 1913, Junius Tribble (J.T.) Rhoton qualified and served as mayor through 1915.

name: Vincenzo borg, c.m.g
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: known as "brared" (1767 - 1837) used this house as his headquarters during the siege of valletta in 1799. on the 9th of february of that year, in the neighbouring battery of ta' twila, "brared" hoisted the british flag for the first time in the history of these islands.

name: Renaker House c
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: 1830. Built for Elijah Kirtley c.1830, probably by Benjamin Platt Fowler, this substantial brick I-House served as the Boone House Tavern until 1870. It later became the residence of Fountain Riddell, attorney, state legislator and founder of the Boone County Deposit Bank, and of Albert Boyers Renaker, Riddell's son-in-law and bank cashier. Boone County bought the building in 1967 and restored it in 1992. Marker placed in 2008.

name: Kilkenny Theatre founded by Richard Power
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Kilkenny Theatre founded by Richard Power. Thomas Moore 1779-1852, The Bard of Erin, performed here 1802-1819.

name: John Adams
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: In gratitude for the Dutch support of the American Revolution In 1782, in this building, John Adams, America's first Ambassador to The Netherlands, met Banker Jan Willink to arrange loans to help establish the independence of The United States. The diplomatic relationship enjoyed today between the two countries is one of America's oldest continuous friendships. Marker placed by National Society Daughters of the American Revolution October 2021.

name: Royal Australasian College of Surgeons
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Architects Leighton, Irwin & Stevenson successfully designed the building for the isolated site which has four visible facades, Built in 1934/35, the design, incorporating coloured brickwork and central massing, won the Royal Victorian Institute of Architects Street Architecture medal in 1937.

name: James F X O'Brien
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: James F X O'Brien 1828-1905 Fenian & MP for Cork & Mayo was born here.

name: Henryton School of Practical Nursing
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: In 1925, two years after the Maryland tuberculosis sanatorium opened in Henryton, a training school for nurses was established for black students in order to help manage the increasing patient population. The program was revised in 1945 to meet licensing standards and opened as the Henryton School of Practical Nursing. A nurses' home constructed in 1952 also housed laboratories, lecture rooms and a library. The school closed in 1963.

name: MAXWELL SIMPSON 1815-1892 Prof
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: of chemistry Queens College (now U.C.C.). First chemist to synthetise succinic acid. He live here 1870-1892.

name: Austin City Limits
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Austin City Limits The longest-running music series in American television history. ACL recorded its first program with WIllie Nelson in October 1974 at KLRU-TV at the University of Texas. Showcasing roots music, legends and innovative popular music from every genre, ACL has become a music icon and helped build Austin's reputation as the "Live Music Capital of the World.".

name: Herman Melville
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Herman Melville author of "Moby Dick" family home 1838-1847 did his earliest writing and completed first two books here, "Typee" and "Omoo".

name: Old City Hall-Fire Station
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Erected 1884. First floor was fire station, with ladder truck, hose wagons and horse stalls. Insignia for the three fire companies appear above doors. Second floor contained city offices. Jail or "calaboose" was in rear. Architect was J. J. Kane. Second story and bell tower were removed in 1933. The Cooke County Heritage Society saved building from demolition, 1966. Renovated through generosity of G. C. and Gladys Morton.

name: David Love Store
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: South Carolina native David M. Love (1821-1892) was an early settler of Williamson County. He was engaged in farming and ranching before moving to Georgetown in the 1860s. A prominent local business leader, he had this Victorian commercial structure built for his mercantile business in the mid-1880s. Features of the building include an ornate metal façade on the second floor, square pilasters, a decorative cornice, and a restored first-floor storefront.

name: The University Club
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This building, inspired by palace architecture of the Italian Renaissance, was designed by McKim, Mead & White and was completed in 1899. Plaque erected 1957 by the New York Community Trust. Landmarks of New York.

name: Heritage Architecture The Gutzlaff Signal Tower
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Heritage Architecture The Gutzlaff Signal Tower. Built in 1907 Reinforced concrete structure.

name: Samuel Curtis 1799-1860
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The renowned Victorian horticulturalist lived here from 1851 and created the extensive landscaped gardens.

name: Thomas House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built in 1827 by John Mitchell and Isaac Lambert for Dr. Pierre Thomas, who acquired the site from the city. The house was remodeled and a new kitchen constructed for Dr. Thomas by Joseph Desjardin in 1844. The Federal-style townhouse remained in the Thomas family until Jean Schweitzer purchased it in 1867 and operated a book and stationery shop here. The cast iron balcony was likely added by Schweitzer.

name: Michael O'Loughlin
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Chief wireless officer operator on the 'S.S. Vestris' went down on the ship while heroically sending out S.O.S. calls 12 Nov 1928 Camolin Parish Homecoming 2018.

name: 700 South Peters
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built in 1910-11 for the Orleans Manufacturing Company. This historic structure is architecturally significant to the Historic Warehouse District, listed in the National Register of Historic Places.

name: The City Of Perth Oldest Building
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The City Of Perth Oldest Building. (1836-37) This building was erected as a Court House between 1836-37. Was designed by Civil Engineer H.W. Reveley and stood close to the Original River Foreshore.

name: Artist Geologist Antiquary
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Artist Geologist Antiquary. Geo V du Noyer 1817-1869 lived here. Recorder of the Past.

name: Kingston Bypass
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Kingston Bypass Officially opened 29 November 2011 by Hon Catherine King, MP PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARY FOR INFRASTRUCTURE AND TRANSPORT Hon Lara Giddings, MP PREMIER OF TASMANIA Hon David O'Byrne MP TASMANIAN MINISTER FOR INFRASTRUCTURE Hon Julie Collins, MP PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARY FOR COMMUNITY SERVICES.

name: The George H
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The George H. Scripps Laboratory Designed by Irving Gill Built 1909-1910 The oldest oceanographic laboratory building in the United States, used for many years as working laboratory, public aquarium classroom and director's office. Many leader in oceanography received their training here. Listed in the National Register of Historic Places Nov. 10, 1977.

name: Charles Robin, 1743-1824
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Merchant and entrepreneur in the Newfoundland cod trade lived here. Founder of a commercial empire in the Gaspé Peninsula, Canada.

name: Fur, Gold, and Cattle
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Founded in 1812, Fort Kamloops stood at a natural crossroads. For 50 years it remained the focus of an inland fur empire until the roaring mining boom of the 1860’s. Ranchers, with cattle and horses, replaced the miners. They settled, and stayed, to see two railways bring prosperity anew to this land of sagebrush, sun, and great rivers.

name: Château Laurier 1908 - 1912
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This dignified hotel was built for the Grand Trunk Railway by the Ottawa Terminals railway company and opened in June 1, 1912. The east wing was added in 1928. Prime minister R.B. Bennett maintained his residence here between 1930 and 1935. Designated Heritage Property / Classé Monument Historique.

name: Kingston City Hall
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built during the mayoralty of John Counter, when Kingston was the capital of the province of Canada. The corner stone was laid by the Governor General, Sir Charles Metcalfe, on June 5, 1843, and the building was completed by November 21, 1844. The architect was George Browne.

name: Charles Borden
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Father of B.C. Archeology Charles Borden (1905 -1978) Investigated the prehistory of Vancouver and the Lower Fraser Valley. His famous excavation at Locarno Beach discovered evidence of human occupation dating back over 3000 years.

name: Aerial Ropeway
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This ropeway was completed in 1904. Its purpose was to convey medical staff, naval patients and stores to the new Royal Navy Hospital built on the mountainside. It also served the Sanitorium on the plateau above the town. The Ropeway ceased to be used in the late 1930's.

name: Lake Mansion Home Of Myron C
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Lake Mansion Home Of Myron C. Lake Founder Of Reno 1877. Built by Washington J. MarshEntrant: National Register of Historic Places.

name: Chollar Mine
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: First located in 1859, the Chollar was consolidated with the Potosi in 1865. As the Chollar-Potosi, it was one of the leading producers on the Comstock. The Nevada mill was erected here in 1887 to process low-grade Chollar ore. It was the last to use the Washoe pan process, but the first on the Comstock to generate and utilize electric power.

name: Panaca Ward Chapel
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: One of the oldest buildings in Lincoln County, the Panaca Ward Chapel was constructed of adobe from the swamps west of town in 1867-1868.Built as a Mormon chapel, the building was also used as a school and recreation hall. The chapel is typical of the development in small Mormon pioneer communities in the intermountain West during the mid-1800s.

name: Bliss Mansion
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: BUILT BY DUANE L. BLISS LUMBER & RAILROAD MAGNATE 1879. In its time the most modern & largest home in Nevada. Entirely constructed of clear lumber & square nails. First home in Nevada entirely piped for gas lighting.

name: The Old Spanish Trail 1829 1850
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The Old Spanish Trail 1829 1850. Stretching for 130 miles across Clark County, this historic horse trail became Nevada’s first route of commerce in 1829 when trade was initiated between Santa Fe and Los Angeles. The trail was later used by the wagons of the “49ers” and by Mormon pioneers. Concrete posts marking the trail were erected in 1965.

name: Old Spanish Trail
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Stretching for 130 miles across Clark County, this historic horse trail became Nevada’s first route of commerce in 1829 when trade was initiated between Santa Fe and Los Angeles. The trail was later used by the wagons of the “49ers” and by Mormon pioneers. Concrete posts marking the trail were erected in 1965.

name: John B. Montgomery
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: On this spot the American Flag was first raised in San Francisco by Commander John B. Montgomery of the U.S.S. Portsmouth July 9 1846 Marked by the Daughters of the American Revolution San Francisco Chapters 1924.

name: North Carolina South Carolina
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: NORTH CAROLINA / Colonized, 1585-87, by first English settlers in America; permanently settled c. 1650; first to vote readiness for independence, Apr. 12, 1776 b/w SOUTH CAROLINA / Formed in 1712 from part of Carolina, which was chartered in 1663, it was first settled by the English in 1670. One of the 13 original states.

name: Rutherford College
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Evolved from private school opened c. 1853 by R. L. Abernethy. Operated 1900-1933 by Methodist Church. Closed 1935. The original site 1.3 mi. N.

name: Fourth Creek Meeting House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Presbyterian. Established ca. 1750; on this site by 1756. The Rev. James Hall first regular minister.

name: William Sharpe 1742 1818
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Member of Continental & provincial congresses; was first legislator to advocate U.N.C., 1784. Grave is 2 miles east.

name: Rocky River Church
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Presbyterian. Founded in early 1750s. Hugh McAden preached here 1755. First regular pastor, Alexander Craighead, 1758. Present church constructed 1860.

name: Plank Road
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This street is the route of the Fayetteville-to-Salem plank road, a toll road 129 miles long, built 1849-54.

name: First Presbyterian Church
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Organized 1816. Site of Constitutional Convention of 1835. State Supreme Court met here, 1831-40, after Capitol fire. This building completed 1900.

name: Charles D. McIver
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Charles D. McIver 1860-1906. Educator and first president of what is now UNC-Greensboro, 1891-1906. Boyhood home is 200 yds. W.

name: Billy Strayhorn 1915 1967
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Jazz composer & pianist. Wrote "Take the A Train" and other songs for Duke Ellington Orchestra. Boyhood home site 1/4 mi. W.

name: John Sprunt Hill 1869 1961
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Banker and attorney. Leader in credit union movement. Benefactor, UNC Library. Lived here.

name: Baron Christoph Von Graffenried
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Was a citizen of Bern, Switzerland. Led Swiss and Palatine immigrants to N.C. where he founded New Bern in 1710.

name: Andrew Cartwright
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Agent of the American Colonization Society in Liberia, founded the A.M.E. Zion churches in Albemarle area. His first church, 1865, near here.

name: Union College
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Union College was incorporated in October 1879. The first degrees were conferred here June 8, 1893. Centennial Hall, formerly known as Classroom Building, was named to the National Register of Historic Places in 1975. Also named to the Register were Speed Hall in 1982 and Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Gymnasium in 1984.

name: Macklin House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This townhouse, built ca. 1850, became home of George B. Macklin, prominent land owner and coal dealer. He came in 1867 from Forks of Elkhorn area. His coal yard near L&N R.R bridge. Two-story brick carriage house at rear, one of few in county, built about same time. Blacksmith shop here also. In Corner of Celebrities Hist. Dist. Presented by John C. Ryan and Donald Duff.

name: Louisville Girls High School
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Serving girls' education for almost 100 years, school was originally known as Female High School and provided women of Louisville with a strong educational base. Opened on April 7, 1856 at Center and Walnut, school functioned on 1st Street and at 5th and Hill before moving to this site in 1934. Architect was J. M. Colley. It consolidated with DuPont Manual Boys School in 1950.

name: Jack Thomas House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: First story, east wing of house, was the earliest brick residence in Grayson County. It was built ca. 1810 by Jack Thomas, first county and circuit court clerk. He added two-story brick wing on north, Federal style. Despite alterations of the 1870s-80s, original walls remain. A striking feature of construction is uniform log joists supporting first floor.

name: Carneal House, ca
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: 1815. Built by Thomas Carneal, a founder of Covington, on land purchased in 1814 from Thomas Kennedy. First brick house in the city. Georgian in concept, style reveals the influence of the great Italian architect Andrea Palladio. In 1825 Lafayette visited as a guest of owner William W. Southgate. Other famous visitors were Henry Clay, Daniel Webster and Andrew Jackson.

name: O'Bannon House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Lt. Presley N. O'Bannon, USMC, the first American to raise our flag on foreign soil, April 17, 1805. Barbary coast pirates who were holding 180 American seamen for ransom were overcome in an attack led by O'Bannon. He came to Logan County in 1807. Served in state legislature 1812, 17, 20-21, and Senate 1824-26. Died in 1850. His remains moved to Frankfort, 1920.

name: Rockcastle County, 1810
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The 52nd Kentucky county created, out of Knox, Lincoln, Madison, Pulaski counties. Isaac Lindsey, who came here with a hunting party in 1767, observed a lone rock which resembled an ancient castle. From this the river was named, later the county. Dr. Thomas Walker and party, first white men to visit the interior of Kentucky, were at this rock as early as 1750.

name: Green County, 1792
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Formed from parts of Lincoln and Nelson counties. The last of seven formed during first legislature. Named for General Nathanael Greene, who, in the Revolutionary War, commanded a unit at Boston, 1776; helped plan defense of New York; fought at Trenton, Brandywine and Monmouth. Sent south by Washington. Greene's Carolina campaign forced British to leave Charleston, 1782.

name: Tanner's Station 1789
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: First settlement in Boone County. The Rev. John Tanner built blockhouse, and town began on 2,000 acres he and John Taylor owned. Shawnees captured Tanner's 9-year-old son here, held him until grown. An ardent Baptist, Tanner preached in Carolinas, Virginia; came to Kentucky in 1781; moved to Missouri, 1798; died there, 1812, age about 80. Town was named Petersburg, 1818.

name: Fleming County
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Kentucky's 26th, was taken out of Mason, 1798. Named for Col. John Fleming who came to area to mark, improve land, 1776. Officer in Rev. War. Built Fleming's Station, second in county, 1788. Closely associated with other pioneers, John Finley, Michael Cassidy, and George Stockton, his halfbrother, who owned the land and who laid out and named Flemingsburg, 1796.

name: County Named, 1798
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: For Edmund Pendleton, 1721-1803. A patriot statesman. Virginian. Member House of Burgesses 1752-1774. In the First Continental Congress. Governor Colonial Virginia 1774-1776. President Virginia Constitutional Convention, 1776, and President of Virginia State Convention that ratified Federal Constitution, 1788. Chief, State Court of Appeals, 1779-1803. County from Bracken and Campbell.

name: Bracken County, 1796
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Formed from parts of Campbell and Mason. Named for William Bracken, hunter, fisherman, Indian fighter, came here 1773. Birthplace of John Gregg Fee, founder of Berea College, 1855. Birthplace and home of Dr. Joshua Taylor Bradford, 1819-71, world famous surgeon. Site Augusta College, first Methodist College in world, 1822. First White Burley tobacco, 1867, from Bracken seed.

name: Old Judge Priest
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Here for six years presided William Sutton Bishop, the famed Judge Priest of Irvin S. Cobb's stories. Judge Bishop, 1839-1902, was First District Circuit Court Judge from 1891 to 1897. Served in 7th Ky. Conf. Inf. "This was a man," Paducah Bar Assn. Presented by Southern Bell Telephone Company.

name: Grayson's Tavern
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Danville's first tavern, operated in this building before 1800 by Benjamin Grayson. Often within these walls the burning political issues of the day were discussed. The Danville Political Society, organized in 1786 and the first of its kind in the West, met and dined here at Grayson's Tavern to "plan the course of the empire" before blazing log fires.

name: Morgan's First Raid
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: CSA General John H. Morgan's first Kentucky raid covered 1,000 miles, July 4 to July 28, 1862-24 days. Left Tenn. with 900 men, returned with 1200, captured 17 towns, 300 horses, destroyed Union supplies. Here, July 21, Morgan took over telegraph line and countermanded USA orders to pursue. Destroyed commissary stores, wagons, arms. Moved on to Monticello. See map. Erected in 1964.

name: Maysville Road
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built by "Maysville and Washington Turnpike Company," incorporated January 29, 1829. First four-mile stretch, Maysville to Washington, was earliest macadamized road in Kentucky and country west of the Alleghenies. Completed November 7, 1830. The road, Lexington to Maysville, was opened to travel in 1835 with thirteen tollhouses and six covered bridges.

name: Dennis Price
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: 23rd June 1915 - 6th October 1973. Dennis Price, English Actor, Television & Film Star. Lived here during the latter years of his life.

name: Forge of Fontenay
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: ASM International has designated Forge of Fontenay An historical landmark "The Forge of Fontenay, erected around 1220 as a part of the Abbey of Fontenay, is the first metallurgical factory in Europe and the palce of the invention of the hydraulic hammer. This invention became the basis of Industrial manufacturing of iron in Europe.".

name: Snaefell Mountain Tramway
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built in just 7 months in 1895, this 5 mile, 3ft. 6ins. (1067mm.) gauge tramway uses the centre rail for emergency breaking on the 1 in 12 gradient.

name: Stephen Daye
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Here lived Stephen Daye who set up nearby the first printing press in British America 1638.

name: Constance Markievicz
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This building housed the department of Labour 1919-1921 Countess Markievicz First Minister for Labour Dail Eireann.

name: Prahran Mechanics' Institute
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Prahran Mechanics' Institute is registered by the Heritage Council of Victoria. This Institute was established in Chapel Street in 1854 to provide education for working class men. This Federation Free Classical style building, designed by Ernest Horatio Willis, was built in 1915 to accommodate the Institute's expansion. Victorian Heritage Register Number H0400.

name: Canterbury Private Hotel
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This building, originally called the Canterbury Club Hotel, was built for William Malone in 1889/90. Its grand design with stables and yard reflected the boom of the late 1880's. The 16 window keystones depict the British Prime Minister, W. E. Gladstone. The hotel was delicenced in 1920 and became a guest house known as Canterbury Mansions.

name: William Brock
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built by Capt William Brock in 1760. Later owned by Capt George Pollard, Junr of the whaling ship "Essex." Herman Melville spoke to Capt Pollard whose story was the basis for "Moby Dick".

name: Pee Wee Saloon
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Pee Wee Saloon (P. Wee Saloon) Pee Wee's Saloon was the favorite meeting spot for Memphis musicians in the early 20th century. W.C. Handy used the cigar counter to write out copies of the Beale Street Blues for his band members. One of those songs, written for the 1909 political campaign was first named "Mr. Crump," for the Memphis mayor and political boss. Later with new lyrics it became famous as "The Memphis Blues.".

name: Rose Cottage
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Rose Cottage (Tigín na Rôs) and the house adjacent to it formed the temporary home of Abbess Mary O'Hagan and six nuns from the Poor Clare Convent who arrived in Kenmare from Newry, Co. Down, in 1861 to found a new convent. Abbess O'Hagan was the sister of Thomas O'Hagan, who became Ireland's first Catholic Lord Chancellor. Her biography was published by Sister Mary Francis Cusack (the 'Nun of Kenmare') in 1877.

name: Jacob von Hogflume
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Swedish Heritage Jacob Von Hogflume Inventor of timetravel lived here in 2193.

name: Denys Corbett Wilson
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: To commemorate the first aeroplane flight between Britain and Ireland by Denys Corbett Wilson. His Bleriot XI landed in this townsland of Crane on April 22nd 1912.

name: Cathedral of Sts Constantine and Helen
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Cathedral of Sts Constantine and Helen. The Cathedral was built by the Hellenic Community of the then Transvaal for worship in the Greek Orthodox tradition. Designed by Hermann Kallenbach in the Byzantine style appropriate to its patron saints, the Cathedral opened its doors on 5 January 1913. It had taken only six years for sufficient funds to be collected from the small Greek community, who were inspired greatly by their spiritual leader, Archimandrite Arthanasios Nikolopoulos.

name: Camp Parapet
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: In 1862 Confederate and Louisiana authorities laid out Camp Parapet as a part of the defense lines of New Orleans. The works were designed to protect the city against an attack from the north. After the Federals, coming up from the south, captured New Orleans, Camp Parapet became an important part of the Union defenses. It served also as a training camp for Northern soldiers.

name: Kellier-Sternberg House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: The Ionic-columned, neoclassical house that once stood here was originally built ca. 1900 for T.G.B. Kellier and was later owned by Edward Sternberg, southeastern claims and litigation manager for the Louisville & Nashville Railroad. In 1999, "The Chimneys" restaurant moved into the house from its former location at the Long Beach Harbor. The house was destroyed by Hurricane Katrina in 2005. Mississippi Department of Archives and History, 2013.

name: Early Long Beach
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: In 1788, Nicholas and Marianne Ladner became the first Europeans to settle in this area. Their log house, known as "The Chimneys", was used as a navigation point for boats traveling from Mobile to New Orleans. After Nicholas's death, the Spanish granted the land to his widow. Much of modern Long Beach includes the Widow Ladner Claim. Mississippi Department of Archives and History, 1999.

name: Saucier-Bidwell-Pratt House
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built ca. 1855 by Pierre Saucier, whose son was later mayor of Pass Christian, the two-story Greek Revival House located here had a central temple-like portico and square-columned galleries spanning its façade, and an octagonal Gothic Revival outbuilding on its grounds. It was later the home of renowned New Orleans theatre impresario David Bidwell. Known locally as "Union Quarters," the house was destroyed during Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

name: Edward Steves Homestead, built 1876
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Given in 1952 by his granddaughter, Edna Steves Vaughan, and her husband, Curtis T. Vaughan. Owned, restores and maintained as a house museum by the San Antonio Conservation Society.

name: The Victoria Hotel
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Built 1873. Built by George Chandler to co-incised with the commencement of the rail service to Benalla in 1873. Originally one storey, a second floor was built in 1913. The Hotel stables building still stands. Chandler had owned and operated an Hotel in Winton.

name: Row Houses
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: This row of Victorian attached cottages were built between 1857 and 1859 for Moses Firth who rented the then eleven cottages out. Shortly afterwards he sold the row to R. Raphael who continued to lease the properties, however by 1880 the number of cottages was reduced to nine. There are now only four remaining from the original row.

name: Town Hall Hotel, Eaglehawk, Victoria
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Town Hall Hotel c1859 In 1859, the hotel's proprietor and publican, Bernard C. McGauran, was offering 'wines and spirits of the best quality, a first class billiard table, and good stabling'. Other publicans have included Henry Lobb and Thomas Chenney. The Town Hall Hotel closed in February 1970. Occupying a prime site in Eaglehawk, the premises have since been used as a nightclub, restaurant, and as a gaming venue known as the Borough Club.

name: Paul Henry
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: Paul Henry 1876 - 1958 Irish artist lived and worked here and at other locations in Achill 1918 - 1919.

name: Richard Cantillon
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: 1680 - 1734) Ballyheigue born "father of modern economics" and the first theorist to define the role of an entrepreneur.

name: Kyneton Savings Bank
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: A savings bank opened in Piper Street in 1861, moved here in 1884, became a branch of the State Savings Bank, then merged with the Commonwealth Bank in 1991. The building is brick with a rendered facing. Notable features are the windows and entrance with classical details and the balustraded parapet above. The design by architects Caselli & Figgis was later used at Maryborough and Warrnambool.

name: Banana Split
subject: Commemorative plaques
text: In 1904 in Latrobe, the first documented Banana Split was created by apprentice pharmacist David Strickler - sold here at the former Tassell Pharmacy.
